notes:
=== CONCEPT ===
-S spoofs the source IP address in outgoing packets. Combined with -e (specify network interface) for routing to a different subnet. When firewall rules block based on source subnet, spoofing a permitted internal IP may bypass the rule.

=== VALIDATION ===
In the CPTS example: port 445 appears 'filtered' from attacker's real IP → -S 10.129.2.200 (spoofed internal IP) → port 445 appears 'open'. Confirms subnet-based firewall ACL.

=== LIMITATION ===
Responses go to the spoofed IP, not the attacker. Attacker only sees RST/SYN-ACK if they can sniff the traffic on the same segment. Works best on local networks where attacker can observe responses via promiscuous mode or ARP poisoning.

=== INTERFACE ===
-e eth0 specifies which interface to send through — required when spoofed IP is on a different subnet than the attacker's default route.
